headline: Coastal Access and Causeway Information
reservation: Park entry fees apply for Andy Bowie County Park and the Isla Blanca area, payable at the gates; no advance reservation system exists for general beach access. Beachfront hotels and campgrounds book up months in advance for March and July. Monitor the official South Padre Island city site for any scheduled maintenance on the Queen Isabella Causeway.

days.title: Wildlife and Wetland Discovery

stops.name: Sea Turtle, Inc.
stops.detail: Visit this rehabilitation center to see rescued Kemp's ridley turtles and learn about Gulf conservation efforts.

stops.name: South Padre Island Birding Center
stops.detail: Walk the extensive boardwalks to spot roseate spoonbills and alligators in the freshwater marshes.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes; local island traffic is generally slow
days.note: Morning is best for bird activity before the afternoon heat sets in.

days.title: Laguna Madre and History

stops.name: Port Isabel Lighthouse
stops.detail: Cross the causeway to climb this historic 1852 beacon for views of the bay and island.

stops.name: Laguna Madre Nature Trail
stops.detail: Explore the bayside boardwalks near the convention center for a quieter, wind-sheltered walking experience.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes including causeway crossing; conditions vary with wind
days.note: The causeway can experience delays during high winds or maritime traffic.

days.title: Northern Dunes and Jetties
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the South End

stops.name: Isla Blanca Park Jetties
stops.detail: Watch for dolphins and large ships entering the Brazos Santiago Pass from the walkable stone jetties.

stops.name: Andy Bowie County Park
stops.detail: Access the more natural, less-developed northern beaches for shelling and viewing the coastal dunes.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes; watch for pedestrians on Gulf Boulevard
days.note: Check beach flag warnings for current rip current and surf conditions.

intel.title: Beach Access Hubs
intel.text: Public beach access lots fill quickly near the central hotels. Use the larger paid lots at Isla Blanca Park for guaranteed space during summer weekends.

intel.title: Coastal Connectivity
intel.text: Signal is strong throughout the town and beaches. Connectivity may drop if you drive significantly north of the pavement into the undeveloped dunes.

intel.title: Island vs Mainland
intel.text: Fuel stations are located along the main island strip, but Port Isabel often offers more competitive pricing. Ensure you have a full tank before exploring the northern beach roads.

intel.title: Spring Break Shifts
intel.text: March brings heavy university crowds and increased traffic. Visit in late April or October for quieter boardwalks and lower humidity.

intel.title: Beach Driving
intel.text: Driving on the sand is permitted only in designated northern zones and requires a permit. Check actual tide charts and soft sand conditions before taking a 2WD vehicle past the pavement.

plan.arrival: Pick up a rental at BRO and drive through Brownsville to Port Isabel for supplies before crossing the 2.5-mile causeway to the island resorts.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for the town and paved roads; a high-clearance 4WD is necessary for exploring the deep sand of North Padre.
plan.goldenHour: The piers along the Laguna Madre offer the best sunset views as the sun dips below the mainland horizon across the water.
